title: Maintenance Operations Coordinator
description:
Maintenance Operations Coordinator (EA-Caliber)

Philippines-based · Full-time · Independent contractor · Maintenance dispatch run to executive-assistant standards of tracking & reporting

Engagement

Independent contractor (you invoice us; you handle your own taxes)

Location

Remote, Philippines-based

Hours

Full shift 2:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. U.S. Pacific (≈ 5:00 p.m. – 2:00 a.m. Philippine Time), Mon–Fri — early hours (2:00–8:00 a.m. PT) for prep and organizing, then live dispatch as the U.S. morning begins; plus available for emergency calls from 9:00 p.m. U.S. Pacific (≈ 12:00 noon Philippine Time)



Reports to

The Owner directly, coordinating closely with our maintenance dispatch lead

Tools provided

AppFolio, Vonage, a shared work-order tracker/schedule, chat (e.g., Viber/WhatsApp),
 & calendar

About Us

A Los Angeles property management company managing a large residential portfolio. Our maintenance operation moves a high volume of work every week, and we need one person to own that pipeline end to end.

The Role

This is a maintenance role run to executive-assistant standards. You dispatch our in-house crew and own the master catalog of every work order — in-house and third-party — with the rigor of a great EA: a flawless tracking system, relentless follow-through until every item closes, and a daily close-out that keeps the Owner fully informed. You run the maintenance operation day to day and report up to the Owner on it. This is not a personal-assistant role — your focus is the maintenance function; the “EA” standard is how well you track, follow through, and report. Nothing falls through the cracks on your watch.

You are the central hub of the maintenance operation. Intake, the dispatch lead, the maintenance coordinator, the portfolio supervisors, the outside-vendor assistant, and the handymen each own a piece — you are the one person who makes sure every piece actually closes. The Owner can turn to you at any moment and get an accurate, complete picture of where everything stands. Your organization and follow-through are what keep the whole team accountable.

You dispatch a crew of 8 in-house handymen and catalog a high volume of work orders each week across the portfolio — plumbing, electrical, carpentry, HVAC, painting, masonry/tiling, and general maintenance. Third-party vendor coordination is handled by a separate assistant; you still ensure their work orders are logged and their status stays current in the master tracker.

What You'll Do

● Own the maintenance inboxes & AppFolio. Monitor the maintenance inbox(es) and AppFolio as the front door for every request — from residents, staff, the answering service, and AppFolio work orders — logging and categorizing each one the moment it arrives so it’s ready to schedule. AppFolio is your system of record.

● Keep the crew fully and productively worked. Proactively plan and assign each of the 8 handymen’s work one to two days ahead — matching jobs to skills, property/location, and priority — so no one is ever sitting idle or unsure what’s next. Rebuild the day when a job falls through, backfilling with the next-priority order, and work closely with the team to keep everyone moving.

● Use the early hours to prepare, then dispatch. Your first block (2:00–8:00 a.m. Pacific) is heads-down prep: review overnight activity, bring the work-order catalog and AppFolio fully current, and build the day’s dispatch plan. As the U.S. morning begins (roughly 8:00–11:00 a.m. Pacific), confirm and send each handyman their schedule, adjust for anything new, and coordinate live.

● Use genuine downtime for back-office support. When the morning prep is done and the crew is dispatched, put spare time toward other work for the Owner — preparing and organizing billing and invoices, reconciling records, drafting correspondence and
s, and similar administrative tasks. This is secondary: it fills real downtime and never comes before dispatch, keeping the catalog current, or emergencies. (You prepare and organize; you do not approve or release any payment.)

● Handle evening & overnight emergencies. You are available for emergency maintenance calls from 9:00 p.m. U.S. Pacific (≈ 12:00 noon your time), and your full shift (2:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. Pacific) covers the overnight tail and the morning dispatch. When an emergency comes in, assess urgency, dispatch the on-call handyman or vendor, keep the resident informed, notify the Owner, and log it.

● Own the master work-order catalog. Make sure every work order — in-house and third-party vendor — is logged, categorized (Electrical, Plumbing, Carpentry, Painting, HVAC, Masonry & Tiling, or General Maintenance), and tracked with status (New, Assigned, Scheduled, Completed), assignee, unit/property, and date. You are the single source of truth for what exists and where it stands.

● Keep vendor orders current (tracking only). The outside-vendor assistant coordinates the vendors; you make sure their work orders are captured in the tracker and their status is updated, so nothing lives outside the catalog.

● Chase everything to closed — and hold the team accountable. Follow up on every open and overdue order, in-house or vendor, until it closes. When a job needs sign-off, route it to the right portfolio supervisor and stay on it until you have their approval. Keep intake, the coordinator, the supervisors, and the handymen moving on their pieces, and escalate high-priority or aging items to the Owner. Treat a second follow-up as an automatic escalation.

● Report like an EA. Send the Owner a daily end-of-shift close-out (what came in, what was dispatched, what’s overdue, tomorrow’s priorities) and a weekly aging review of anything not yet closed, plus monthly volume/vendor reporting. The Owner should never have to ask where something stands.

● Communicate & coordinate across the team. Work hand in hand with Maintenance Intake, the Maintenance Coordinator, the dispatch lead, the portfolio supervisors, and the outside-vendor assistant. Draft maintenance
s during the early block for the team to send when the U.S. day begins, handle maintenance correspondence with residents, staff, and vendors clearly and professionally, and keep the Owner informed with discretion on resident and personnel matters.

What We're Looking For

The one thing that matters most: this role lives or dies on follow-through. We are looking for someone with a proven, flawless system for tracking every open item to completion. Expect to describe it in your application and demonstrate it live in the interview.

● A flawless tracking system — the most important trait. You run every work order and every handyman’s schedule through a real, disciplined system with a defined tool and daily routine — never your memory. Nothing you are responsible for is ever lost or forgotten. In the interview you will be asked to show us this system and walk through what’s open on it right now.

● EA-level communication & reporting. You write clearly and professionally enough to correspond with residents, staff, and vendors and to produce a clean, useful daily close-out for the Owner.

● Closure mindset. You are wired to chase open items to done and escalate the moment something stalls — you find satisfaction in an empty overdue list, not just a busy day.

● A hub, not a silo. You are comfortable being the person everyone else’s work routes through — coordinating across intake, supervisors, vendors, and the crew, and politely holding people accountable to their part without friction.

● Proactive, not reactive. You get ahead of the work — the crew always knows what’s next and approvals are chased before they become blockers — rather than waiting to be asked.

● High-volume accuracy — you manage many concurrent, detail-sensitive orders and 8 people’s schedules without losing track or making errors.

● Clear spoken English — you’ll coordinate with handymen, residents, and staff by phone and chat every day, including calm handling of overnight and early-morning emergency calls. This is load-bearing, not optional.

● Strong written English — clear reports and correspondence to leadership, vendors, and residents.

● Comfort directing and following up — confidently assigning work to the crew and staying on an order until it’s done.

● Spreadsheet skill — Excel or Google Sheets (filtering, formulas, pivot tables); AppFolio experience a strong plus.

● Construction or trades knowledge — a background in construction, a skilled trade, or hands-on maintenance so you understand the work being dispatched: what a job actually involves, roughly how long it should take, what materials or specialty vendor it needs, and whether something is routine or an emergency.

● A plus: hands-on construction or skilled-trade experience (or having run a crew); prior experience dispatching or scheduling a field crew, or supporting a maintenance, facilities, or property-management function.

The Boundaries of This Role

For clarity and trust, this role explicitly does NOT include:

● Approval authority over money — you prepare and reconcile invoices; you do not approve, release, or make payments.

● Banking-portal access, wire initiation, check printing, or card credentials.

● Signature authority or committing the company to vendor contracts.

● Legal or rent-control work product; owner-relationship or commercial-terms decisions.

What Success Looks Like

● Work orders move New → Assigned → Scheduled → Completed with minimal delay and none falling through the cracks.

● The Owner and dispatch lead always have one accurate, up-to-date picture of every open order — in-house and vendor — by category, property, and status.

● The 8 handymen stay productively scheduled a day or two ahead, with same-day gaps filled quickly and end-of-day status captured.

● Every request is captured at intake, and after-hours emergencies are handled quickly and calmly — dispatched, logged, and escalated to the Owner.

How to Apply — Read Carefully

To be considered, your application MUST include all of the following. Applications missing any item will not be reviewed.

#

Include with your application

1

Internet speed proof — a Speedtest.net screenshot showing at least 25 Mbps download.

2

Your system (most important) — in your own words, describe in detail the exact system you use so that nothing you are responsible for is ever forgotten — specifically how you would schedule 8 people’s daily work and track every open work order from intake to completion. Name the tool, the routine, and how you know at a glance what is still open or overdue. If you advance, you will walk us through this system live.

3

A short judgment answer — Two quick scenarios: (a) You’re preparing the morning dispatch and one of the 8 handymen calls in sick while a resident reports no hot water — how do you re-plan the day? (b) It’s 3:00 a.m. Pacific and a resident calls reporting water leaking from the ceiling — what do you do?

4

Two short answers — (a) Describe your experience scheduling people, dispatching a crew, or coordinating high-volume work orders. (b) Your internet provider and backup plan for outages.

5

Your rate in USD and earliest availability.

Why these? They mirror the actual work. Strong applications move to a short skills exercise, a video interview, and reference checks.

Our Process

● Application review against the requirements above.

● Skills exercise (a realistic dispatch + work-order tracking exercise).

● Video interview (including a short phone role-play) · reference checks · offer.

title: Wikipedia Page Specialist (Freelance/Project-Based)
description:
About Chado Trading



Chado Trading hires for the long term. We have several team members from OnlineJobs.ph who've been with us for 5+ years, and we're looking for someone who wants a lasting working relationship, not a one-off gig. Integrity and honesty matter a lot to us - we want someone who does careful, above-board work and is upfront with us, especially given the nature of Wikipedia's editorial standards.



About the Role



We already have the content and sources prepared for the subject (a tea pioneer and scholar). What we need is someone who knows how to properly format, structure, and submit this material as a compliant Wikipedia entry. This isn't a research-from-scratch role; it's about taking material we provide and shaping it into something that meets Wikipedia's editorial and sourcing standards, then successfully navigating it through review.



Key Responsibilities



Notability Check: Review the content and sources we provide against Wikipedia's notability guidelines for biographies (WP:BIO / WP:GNG) and flag early if anything is likely to be contested, before drafting begins.



Content Adaptation: Take the content and sources we supply and restructure/rewrite them into a neutral, encyclopedic Wikipedia entry — correct tone, structure, and formatting per Wikipedia conventions.



Source Formatting: Format and cite our provided sources correctly per Wikipedia's citation standards, and confirm each one meets the "independent, reliable secondary source" bar — flagging any that may not hold up under review.



Submission & Mediation: Manage the "Articles for Creation" (AfC) process and respond professionally to reviewer feedback or community edits.



Compliance: Strictly follow Wikipedia's Conflict of Interest (COI) disclosure requirements and Neutral Point of View (NPOV) policy, since these entries are being created on behalf of a company/client.



Requirements & Experience



Proven track record of Wikipedia pages you've successfully gotten published and kept live, ideally for individuals or companies.



Solid working knowledge of Wikipedia's Five Pillars and what counts as a "reliable source."



Ability to rewrite provided material into a neutral, journalistic tone — no promotional or marketing language.



Comfortable with Wiki-markup or VisualEditor and familiar with how the Wikipedia editor community operates.



Honest, reliable, and comfortable being transparent with us about process, sourcing, and any issues that come up along the way.



Room to Grow



This role can expand well beyond Wikipedia work. Right after this batch of articles, there's recurring work available administering and posting content for the websites in our portfolio companies. Beyond that, if you show interest, Chado Trading is genuinely happy to teach you about the tea industry itself - we like bringing people in who want to grow with the company into other roles over time, not just complete a task list.



How to Apply



Please send your portfolio of published Wikipedia articles (links to live pages, not drafts that were deleted/rejected), a short note on your experience with AfC submissions, and your proposed rate per article. Let us know too if you're interested in long-term work beyond this project.

title: AI Video Producer & Cinematic Content Creator — EV Studios.
description:
EV Studios is building a cinematic, AI-driven creative ecosystem supporting a growing portfolio of brands across media, SaaS, local business, education, advertising, entertainment, and digital ventures.



We’re looking for a highly creative, multi-skilled AI Video Creator, Editor & Graphic Designer who understands that great creative work is more than technically editing clips — it is about storytelling, emotion, pacing, composition, branding, and capturing attention.



This is not a basic Canva or social-media editing position. We want someone excited about combining traditional creative skills with the newest generation of AI production tools to create work that increasingly approaches commercial and cinematic production quality.



What You’ll Do

Create and edit cinematic commercials, brand films, social content, short-form video, promotional pieces, and advertising creative

Work with leading and emerging AI video/image platforms such as Higgsfield, Runway, Sora, Kling, Veo, Pika, Midjourney, ChatGPT image generation, and whatever powerful tools emerge next

Edit and finish productions using Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, or comparable professional tools

Create compelling graphics, advertisements, thumbnails, social assets, brand collateral, and visual campaigns

Help develop and maintain visual identities, logos, typography, and brand systems

Combine AI-generated material with real photography, video, voice, music, graphics, and traditional editing

Collaborate on concepts, scripts, storyboards, shot development, and visual storytelling

Maintain consistency across EV Studios and our expanding ecosystem of brands

Experiment constantly with new AI creative technology and help us determine which tools genuinely improve production

Help develop repeatable AI-assisted production workflows that allow us to produce exceptional creative work efficiently



GoHighLevel experience is required. You should be comfortable working within GHL and incorporating finished creative assets into websites, funnels, campaigns, and related brand systems.



Must be skilled at taking real, raw footage from videographers and seamlessly integrating AI for effects, color grading, enhancement, narration, supplemental footage, scene modification, sound, and other post-production needs. The goal is to blend real-world cinematography with AI tools to transform raw footage into polished, professional, cinematic finished productions. 

Must have comprehensive, hands-on experience with leading AI video platforms, particularly Higgsfield and HeyGen, along with Runway, Google Veo, and Kling. We’re looking for someone who understands how to choose and combine the strengths of different AI tools within a professional production workflow—not someone who has simply experimented with them.



What We’re Looking For



You should have strong demonstrated ability in:



Video editing and visual storytelling

AI video and image generation

Motion graphics and compositing

Graphic design

Photoshop, Figma, Canva and/or comparable design software

Professional video editing software

Brand identity and visual consistency

Prompting and directing generative AI

Sound, music, pacing and emotional rhythm

Understanding what makes advertising creative actually hold attention



Experience with brand development, logo design, cinematography, photography, color grading, sound design, or commercial advertising is a major plus.



More important than knowing every tool is having excellent visual judgment and the ability to learn new technology quickly.



Who Will Thrive Here



We want someone who sees AI as an expansion of creativity rather than a shortcut around creativity.



You should be curious enough to experiment, disciplined enough to finish polished work, and opinionated enough to say when something doesn't look good, even if AI generated it.



We're particularly interested in someone who wants to grow beyond being an editor and eventually take ownership of productions, creative direction, and other creators.



Opportunity



This is an opportunity to work across an unusually diverse portfolio rather than producing variations of the same content every day.



You'll have:



Exposure to multiple businesses, industries and creative formats

Access to advanced AI creative tools and experimentation

Opportunities to develop new production workflows

Increasing creative responsibility

A potential path toward Lead Visual Producer / Creative Director as EV Studios grows



How to Apply

Please send:

Examples of your best AI-generated video or visual work

Which AI creative tools you currently use and which you consider yourself strongest with

In this role, you would be responsible for solving the ongoing puzzle of ensuring our global supply chain is well stocked with profitable items that well serve evolving customer and industry trends. This position requires an individual who is a thoughtful, resourceful, positive communicator with a strong interest in data science and always-evolving analytics that also enjoys solving problems under his or her own initiative to help plan our global inventory needs.



Job Responsibilities:

> Utilize historical sales trend and weekly sell-thru reporting to develop and execute weekly demand planning for each of our global sales channels including brick-and-mortal retail, wholesale, and online eCommerce.

> Compile and review weekly reporting on sales performance and inventory distribution metrics.

Forecast and manage global inventory data to ensure all required stock level goals are regularly maintained.

> Manage excess & obsolete (E&O) inventory and propose action plans to mitigate risk, meet and exceed inventory health targets, and ensure maximum profitability.

> Analyze current warehouse capacity constraints and vendor order requirements such as lead-times and minimum order quantity to develop inventory purchasing forecasts.

> Assist the Accounting department with ongoing audits, inventory control, and reconciliations.

> Analyze performance of sales growth, eCommerce PPC campaigns, lead generation, and other advertising campaigns and suggest strategies for improvement based on your ongoing analysis of how these sales activities affect inventory sell-through and the global supply chain.

> Diagnose and assist with time sensitive issues relating to data errors and impact on sales trends.



Basic Requirements:

> Education: College degree in business, finance, data science, or related fields of study.

> At least 2 years experience in consumer goods demand planning or inventory/sales forecasting.

> Deep analytical skills and a strong problem-solving ability.

> Strong bias for action with ability to prioritize, multi-task, tenaciously follow-up, and meet > competing deadlines.

> Advanced skills in Microsoft Office including Excel (Advanced Formulas, Tables & Formatting, Conditional Formatting, Advanced Charting, Pivot tables & Pivot Reporting, VLOOKUP, etc).

> Excellent oral and written communication skills.

> Advanced analytical skills and attention to detail.



Accessory Power is a consumer electronics manufacturer dedicated to providing a diverse range of high quality products for over 30 years. We manufacture and market thousands of products under our four main brands: GOgroove® | ENHANCE® | ReVIVE® | USA Gear® along with a handful of other lines and various accessory products. We would love to grow together!



Visit accessorypower.com to about to learn a little more about our incredible past and our bright future ahead.

electronic health record (EHR) systems.

• Assist patients with appointment scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellations.

• Navigate provider schedules and select the appropriate appointment type, provider, date, and time based on the patient’s needs.

• Verify and update patient demographics, contact information, date of birth, and other registration details.

• Verify and update patient insurance information and assist with basic insurance eligibility-related tasks.

• Perform other administrative and patient-support duties as assigned.



EHR/EMR Experience – Required

Candidates must be comfortable navigating and working within an EHR/EMR system.

Experience should include, but is not limited to:

• Searching for and locating patient charts.

• Reviewing patient demographics and medical information.

• Updating patient information and insurance details.

• Documenting telephone encounters and patient messages.

• Reviewing provider schedules and appointment availability.

• Scheduling, rescheduling, and canceling appointments.

• Selecting the appropriate provider and appointment type.

• Reviewing previous encounters, notes, orders, referrals, and other relevant chart

information.

• Entering accurate documentation while maintaining patient privacy.

Experience with any of the following systems is highly preferred:

• ModMed / Modernizing Medicine

• eClinicalWorks (eCW)

• Other U.S. healthcare EHR/EMR systems



Required Qualifications

• 2+ years of experience working in a U.S. healthcare environment preferred.

• Must be fluent in English, Spanish ideal

• Previous experience as a Virtual Medical Assistant, Medical Assistant, Medical Receptionist, Patient Service Representative, Medical Scheduler, or similar healthcare position.

• Hands-on experience with patient scheduling and appointment management.

• Strong knowledge of U.S. healthcare workflows and patient-care processes.

• Hands-on experience using EHR/EMR systems.

• Experience with ModMed, eCW, or similar platforms is highly preferred.

• Experience handling patient calls and communicating directly with U.S. patients.

• Basic understanding of U.S. health insurance, including Medicare, Medicaid, HMO, PPO, commercial insurance, referrals, and eligibility.

• Working knowledge of medical terminology.

• Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

• Ability to multitask while maintaining high-quality patient service.

• Ability to work independently and effectively in a remote environment.



Preferred Healthcare Experience

Experience in any of the following areas is highly preferred:

• Patient scheduling and appointment coordination

• EHR/EMR navigation and documentation

• Insurance verification and eligibility

• Patient registration

• Referral and authorization workflows

• Prescription refill requests

• Nurse message-taking

• Medical records and chart management

• Gastroenterology

• Specialty medical practices

• U.S. physician offices and outpatient clinics



Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone who has real, hands-on U.S. healthcare experience and can confidently support patients and medical-office operations.

The ideal candidate:

• Understands how a U.S. medical office operates.

• Is experienced in working directly with U.S. patients.

• Can confidently navigate an EHR and locate the information needed to assist a patient.

• Can accurately schedule appointments based on the reason for visit, provider, appointment type, and availability.

• Can document patient interactions clearly and accurately.

• Can quickly learn new EHR systems and healthcare platforms.

• Understands the importance of HIPAA, patient privacy, and accurate documentation.

• Demonstrates professionalism, empathy, patience, and excellent communication skills.

• Is dependable, detail-oriented, and capable of working independently

description:

Responsibilities include:



-Consistently call and follow up with Day 2+ mortgage leads

-Work through assigned lead lists each day

-Follow up with long-term leads after priority leads have been contacted

-Use provided voi
 and text follow-up templates

-Ask interested prospects questions from a provided Lead Intake Form

-Take detailed and accurate notes from every meaningful conversation

-Enter and maintain lead information in the CRM

-Keep lead statuses organized and up to date

-Schedule interested prospects directly onto my calendar

-Communicate with me when a lead needs my attention

-Track working hours accurately



Schedule: I am looking for someone who can work a minimum of 4-6 hours per day Monday - Saturday, with the opportunity to work additional hours when needed. 



Because speed-to-lead is extremely important, your working hours will need to overlap with U.S. business hours.



The right person should be:



* Fluent and confident in spoken English

* Comfortable spending a significant portion of the day on the phone

* Comfortable making outbound calls

* Friendly, professional, and conversational

* Able to follow a defined process consistently

* Organized and detail-oriented

* Good at taking detailed notes

* Comfortable learning CRM and dialing software

* Responsive when communicating with me

* Self-motivated and able to stay productive without constant supervision

* Reliable with a stable internet connection and quiet calling environment

* Outbound calling

* Lead generation

* Appointment setting

* CRM management

* U.S.-based customer service

* Sales development or follow-up

I am looking for someone who can potentially become a long-term part of my business, not someone looking for a short-term project. To show that you read the entire job posting, start your application with the words “Day 2 Follow Up.” Do not mention these instructions anywhere else in your application. Also include a 30–60 second voice recording introducing yourself and explaining your previous phone experience.

description:
Remote | Part-Time to Start | U.S.-Credentialed RDs/RDNs Based in the Philippines Encouraged to Apply



Happy Health & Nutrition (HHN) is a growing U.S.-based virtual nutrition and health-coaching organization seeking an exceptional Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) to help us build and manage the clinical documentation and physician-communication infrastructure behind our care.



This is not a traditional full-time coaching position.



It is a behind-the-scenes clinical role for an RDN who enjoys:



* understanding complex patient journeys;

* finding the clinically meaningful story inside extensive session information;

* reviewing AI-assisted documentation critically rather than blindly accepting it;

* improving clinical systems;

* recognizing when something requires escalation;

* and making sure referring physicians remain meaningfully connected to what is happening with their patients.



At HHN, our coaches often see what happens between medical visits.



Your job will help make sure those important developments do not disappear inside a transcript, an isolated progress note, or a conversation that never reaches the referring provider.



⸻



Your Primary Outcome



Every HHN client journey should be clinically coherent, accurately documented, appropriately escalated, and meaningfully communicated to the healthcare professionals involved in their care.



You are not being hired simply to make notes sound better.



You will help HHN build a reliable clinical communication system that allows us to answer:



What is changing with this patient?



What is helping?



What is getting in the way?



Is there anything clinically important the RDN or physician should know?



What should happen next?



As the role develops, you may become the person responsible for ensuring that referring providers receive thoughtful, timely communication about their patients—including planned longitudinal and quarterly progress updates.



⸻



What You Will Own



1. Clinical Documentation Quality



You will review information from nutrition and health-coaching encounters and help create accurate, concise, clinically useful documentation.



Responsibilities may include:



* Reviewing nutrition and coaching session transcripts and documentation.

* Extracting clinically meaningful information from extensive conversations.

* Reviewing AI-generated clinical documentation for accuracy, omissions, unsupported assumptions, and inappropriate conclusions.

* Ensuring notes accurately reflect what occurred during the encounter.

* Identifying meaningful changes in symptoms, nutrition, medications, laboratory values, weight, function, behavior, and treatment barriers.

* Ensuring interventions, goals, progress, barriers, and follow-up needs are clearly documented.

* Returning incomplete information for clarification rather than filling gaps with assumptions.

* Reviewing longitudinal records so important developments are not lost between visits.



⸻



2. AI-Assisted Clinical Documentation Systems



HHN is actively developing AI-assisted workflows to improve clinical documentation without compromising clinical judgment or documentation integrity.



You will help us:



* Work within healthcare AI documentation and medical-scribe technology.

* Build and refine clinical templates, note formats, standards, and workflows.

* Translate HHN documentation standards into repeatable AI-assisted processes.

* Test AI outputs against the source encounter.

* Identify hallucinations, unsupported assumptions, omissions, or misleading language.

* Improve prompts, templates, and workflows when recurring documentation problems appear.

* Help determine what AI can appropriately automate—and what must remain under human clinical review.

* Participate in quality-control testing as our systems evolve.



We are not looking for someone who trusts AI because it sounds convincing.



We are looking for someone who can recognize when AI is wrong.



The technology can be learned.



Clinical judgment cannot be outsourced.



⸻



3. Clinical Continuity & Escalation



You will help us understand the patient’s larger clinical story—not simply the latest visit.



You may review:



* medication changes;

* emerging GI symptoms;

* nutrition adequacy;

* weight and body-composition concerns;

* laboratory trends;

* diabetes and glucose patterns;

* cardiovascular risk;

* functional changes;

* significant behavioral barriers;

* treatment adherence;

* changes in appetite;

* life circumstances affecting treatment;

* and other developments relevant to nutrition care.



You will help determine when information requires:



* clarification from the coach;

* review by the supervising RDN;

* communication with the referring provider;

* or another appropriate escalation pathway.



You will never be expected to diagnose outside your scope or invent clinical conclusions the record does not support.



⸻



4. Physician & Referral-Partner Communication



This is a major part of the long-term vision for this role.



HHN wants referring healthcare professionals to know that when they entrust us with a patient, the communication loop does not disappear.



You will help:



* Prepare concise physician-facing progress updates.

* Distinguish what a physician needs to know from information that belongs only in the internal clinical record.

* Identify meaningful milestones and barriers worth communicating.

* Maintain consistency in provider communication.

* Track when updates were sent and when the next communication is due.

* Support initial referral loop-backs and longitudinal progress communication.

* Eventually help manage planned quarterly updates for referring providers with active HHN patients.



Our goal is not to overwhelm physicians with documentation.



Our goal is to help them quickly understand:



Did my patient engage?



Are they progressing?



What has changed?



What is getting in the way?



Is anything clinically important emerging?



What is HHN doing next?



⸻



5. Clinical Quality Improvement



We do not want someone who simply fixes the same documentation problem every week.



We want someone who asks:



“Why does this problem keep happening—and how do we improve the system?”



You may help:



* Maintain HHN clinical documentation standards.

* Develop templates, checklists, and quality-control processes.

* Identify recurring documentation weaknesses.

* Track common coaching/documentation misses.

* Help turn recurring problems into coach education.

* Participate in case review and clinical-quality meetings.

* Recommend workflow improvements.

* Help HHN continuously strengthen the quality of care as the organization grows.



⸻



Documentation Integrity Is Non-Negotiable



This role is about accurately representing care that actually occurred.



You will never be expected to:



* fabricate information;

* backfill unsupported details;

* invent an intervention;

* assume a medication change occurred;

* manufacture clinical findings;

* or alter the substance of an encounter merely to make a note appear stronger.



If something important cannot be established from the information available, the correct response may be:



“The record does not establish this. I need clarification before documenting it.”



We value that judgment enormously.



⸻



Required Qualifications



You must currently hold:



An active U.S. RD or RDN credential through the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR).



Please be prepared to provide credential verification during the selection process.



We especially welcome U.S.-credentialed RDs/RDNs currently residing in the Philippines.



An active Philippine PRC Nutritionist-Dietitian license is highly valued, but the Philippine credential alone does not replace the U.S. CDR requirement for this position.



You should also demonstrate:



* Exceptional written English.

* Strong clinical reasoning.

* Excellent attention to detail.

* Ability to synthesize large amounts of information.

* Ability to distinguish clinically meaningful information from conversational detail.

* Sound professional judgment regarding escalation.

* Strong organization and follow-through.

* Comfort learning technology quickly.

* Curiosity about AI-assisted healthcare workflows.

* Ability to work independently without working silently when something is unclear.

* High regard for confidentiality and HIPAA-compliant workflows.

* Ability to receive feedback without defensiveness and use it to improve.

* Reliability with deadlines and recurring responsibilities.



⸻



Strongly Preferred Experience



We would especially like to hear from RDNs with experience in:



* physician offices;

* obesity medicine;

* anti-obesity medication / GLP-1 care;

* endocrinology;

* diabetes;

* bariatrics;

* gastroenterology;

* metabolic health;

* cardiovascular risk;

* primary care;

* medical nutrition therapy;

* clinical nutrition;

* chart review;

* documentation auditing;

* quality assurance;

* physician progress notes;

* referral communication;

* multidisciplinary care;

* healthcare AI;

* medical scribe technology;

* or clinical workflow automation.



Advanced credentials such as CDCES or similar clinical certifications are welcome.



Prior experience with a specific AI platform is not required.



We care more about whether you understand how to evaluate clinical AI critically.



⸻



Who Will Thrive in This Role



You may love this role if you naturally think:



“Wait—what happened to this patient’s A1c?”



“Was the medication actually changed, or are we assuming that?”



“The patient lost weight, but how are they eating?”



“The physician needs to know this.”



“The note says the client improved. What specifically improved?”



“There are three months of meaningful progress here, but the current note does not make the journey visible.”



“The AI wrote that—but the transcript doesn’t support it.”



“Before I finalize this, I need clarification.”



You enjoy clinical detective work.



You notice patterns.



You ask thoughtful questions.



You care about accuracy.



You like creating order from complexity.



You do not need to be the loudest person in the room.



You need to be the person who notices what everyone else missed.



⸻



This Role Is Probably Not for You If



Please do not apply if:



* You are primarily seeking a patient-facing counseling role.

* You do not currently hold the required U.S. CDR credential.

* You dislike reviewing charts, transcripts, or longitudinal patient information.

* You routinely fill in missing information because something “probably happened.”

* You assume AI-generated documentation is accurate because it sounds professional.

* You hesitate to ask for clarification.

* You need highly detailed instructions for every decision.

* You regularly miss deadlines.

* You wait until a problem becomes serious before communicating it.

* You prefer completing assigned tasks without understanding why the task matters.

* You become defensive when your work is questioned or corrected.



Our standards are high because patients and healthcare professionals depend on the quality of our work.



⸻



What It Feels Like to Work at HHN



HHN is growing, but we do not want growth to cost us the human connection that made our work meaningful in the first place.



We are building a team where people know that their work matters, their judgment matters, and their development matters.



We want HHN to feel like a professional community—not a collection of people completing disconnected tasks from different computers.



You will work alongside people who care deeply about patients, about one another, and about becoming better at what we do.



We learn together.



We discuss difficult cases.



We ask questions.



We share what worked.



We admit when something did not work.



We improve the system instead of hiding the problem.



We celebrate meaningful patient progress.



And we expect every team member to understand that their work affects the work of everyone who comes after them.



⸻



Our Core Values



See the Whole Person



A diagnosis, body weight, laboratory result, or progress note never tells the entire story.



We remain curious about the person behind the data.



Consistency Over Perfection



We do not expect patients—or teammates—to be perfect.



We expect people to return, learn, improve, and keep moving forward.



Clinical Integrity



We document what happened.



We distinguish evidence from assumptions.



We raise concerns when something does not look right.



We do not sacrifice accuracy for convenience.



Ownership



We do not simply ask:



“Did I complete my task?”



We ask:



“Did the outcome actually happen?”



If something is unclear, broken, delayed, or at risk, we communicate early.



Continuous Improvement



Problems are information.



When something fails, we do not merely fix today’s instance.



We ask how the system should change so tomorrow is better.



Collaboration



Exceptional care is rarely created by one person.



We respect the expertise of coaches, dietitians, physicians, psychologists, administrative professionals, and the patient themselves.



We close communication loops.



Develop Independence, Not Dependence



Our goal is not to make patients need us forever.



Our goal is to help people become increasingly capable of navigating their own health.



We bring that same philosophy to our team: we teach, develop, and trust people to grow.



⸻



How We Work Together



At HHN, strong team members:



* understand the outcome behind the assignment;

* ask questions when something does not make sense;

* communicate problems early;

* follow through on commitments;

* welcome thoughtful feedback;

* contribute ideas;

* protect patient confidentiality;

* help teammates succeed;

* and leave systems better than they found them.



You will not be expected to know everything on Day 1.



You will be expected to be curious, responsible, teachable, and committed to excellence.



⸻



Schedule



Remote | Part-Time to Start



Much of the documentation work may be completed asynchronously.



Some overlap with U.S. Central Time will be required for:



* clinical case review;

* quality meetings;

* training;

* provider-communication planning;

* and team collaboration.



Applicants should clearly state their reliable availability in U.S. Central Time.



The role may expand as HHN grows and based on demonstrated ability.



⸻



Compensation



This is a paid professional position.



Compensation will reflect:



* credentials;

* relevant experience;

* demonstrated clinical judgment;

* technical/system capability;

* expected hours;

* and final scope of responsibility.



Qualified candidates will receive compensation information before completing the final hiring stage.



⸻



How to Apply



Please submit your résumé/CV and answer every question below.



Applications that do not follow the instructions may not advance.



Begin your application with:



“Clinical continuity matters because…”



Complete that sentence in your own words.



Then answer:



1.



Do you currently hold an active RD or RDN credential through the U.S. Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR)?



State your exact credential and current status.



2.



Do you currently hold an active Philippine PRC Nutritionist-Dietitian license or another professional nutrition/dietetics license?



List each credential and status.



3.



Describe your experience writing, reviewing, or auditing clinical progress notes.



What exactly were you responsible for?



4.



Have you worked directly with physicians, medical practices, or multidisciplinary healthcare teams?



If yes, explain how patient progress, barriers, or clinical concerns were communicated.



5.



Which clinical populations have you worked with most extensively?



6.



Tell us about a time you identified an important clinical detail, inconsistency, or risk that another person had overlooked.



What did you notice?



What did you do?



7.



Tell us about a time when you did not have enough information to accurately complete clinical work.



How did you handle it?



8.



Which AI-assisted healthcare documentation, medical-scribe, clinical decision-support, or healthcare workflow tools have you used?



For each, briefly explain:



* what you used it for;

* what it did well;

* where you found it unreliable or limited;

* and how you verified its output.



If you have not used healthcare AI yet, tell us about another complex technology you learned quickly.



9.



Have you ever identified an error, unsupported assumption, or meaningful omission in AI-generated content?



If yes, describe what happened.



10.



Imagine an AI-generated progress note says:



“Patient is meeting protein needs and tolerating medication well.”



The source transcript shows the patient saying only:



“I’ve been trying to eat more protein. The medication has been okay, I guess.”



What would you do before finalizing the note?



11.



What hours are you reliably available in U.S. Central Time?



12.



Why does this role interest you more than a traditional patient-facing RDN position?



13.



What kind of professional environment helps you do your best work?



14.



Tell us about a system or process you improved—not merely a task you completed.



What problem did you notice, and what changed because of your work?



⸻



Our Selection Process



We care much more about demonstrated ability than polished interviewing.



Qualified candidates should expect:



Stage 1 — Application Review



We evaluate:



* required credentials;

* ability to follow instructions;

* written communication;

* relevant experience;

* clinical reasoning;

* technology curiosity;

* and alignment with HHN culture.



Stage 2 — Short Screening Conversation



We assess:



* communication;

* role expectations;

* reliability;

* values;

* availability;

* and fit.



Stage 3 — Paid Clinical & AI Competency Exercise



Selected finalists will receive:



* a de-identified patient/session transcript;

* an HHN documentation standard;

* an AI-generated draft note;

* and a physician-update scenario.



You may be asked to:



1. Audit the AI-generated note.

2. Create the final internal clinical progress note.

3. Prepare a concise physician-facing update.

4. Identify missing information.

5. Identify unsupported AI assumptions.

6. Identify anything requiring clinical escalation.

7. Explain what you would change in the documentation workflow to prevent recurring errors.



Stage 4 — Final Interview



We discuss your clinical judgment, work sample, systems thinking, development goals, and what it would look like to grow together at HHN.



⸻



Where This Role Can Grow



For the right person, this position can become significantly larger than documentation review.



A high-performing RDN could eventually help lead HHN’s clinical-quality infrastructure across:



Clinical Documentation

AI Workflow Governance

Provider Communication

Clinical Quality Assurance

Case Review

Coach Development

Referral-Partner Communication Standards



Over time, this person could potentially grow toward a role such as:



Clinical Quality & Provider Communication Lead



We are building for the long term.



We are looking for someone who wants to help build with us.



⸻



A Final Note



HHN is not looking for someone who simply wants another remote job.



We are looking for someone who cares about the details that protect excellent patient care.



Someone who wants their work to mean something.



Someone who enjoys learning alongside a team.



Someone who can see both the patient and the system surrounding the patient.



And someone who wants to help us build a healthcare organization where excellent coaching, sound clinical judgment, responsible technology, and meaningful physician collaboration can exist together.



If that sounds like the kind of work—and the kind of professional community—you have been looking for, we would love to hear from you.



Happy Health & Nutrition

title: Customer Service & Scheduling Specialist (Phone + Email | US Clients | Full-Time)
description:
We are looking for a detail-oriented Customer Service & Scheduling Specialist to manage existing client communication, scheduling adjustments, and daily service coordination.



This role is critical to ensuring our operations run smoothly and customers receive excellent service.



You will be speaking with U.S.-based clients, so clear, professional English is required.



Key Responsibilities

-Handle inbound customer calls and messages

-Manage reschedules, cancellations, and service updates

-Confirm upcoming appointments with clients

-Coordinate schedules to maximize efficiency

-Communicate clearly with internal team regarding changes

-Maintain accurate records in our system



What Success Looks Like (KPIs)

You will be measured on:

-Schedule Efficiency: % of available time filled

-Cancellation Rate: Minimize lost revenue from cancellations

-Response Time: Fast, professional communication

-Accuracy: Minimal errors in scheduling and updates



Requirements

-Strong spoken and written English (neutral/minimal accent preferred)

-Calm, professional communication style

-Highly organized and detail-oriented

-Able to manage multiple conversations/tasks at once

-Reliable internet and quiet workspace

-Available during U.S. business hours



Compensation

-$3–$6/hour



Performance bonuses tied to:

-Low cancellation rates

-High schedule utilization



Why Join Us

-Stable, long-term role

-Structured systems and processes

-Supportive team environment

-Opportunity to grow into operations role



Application Instructions

Please include:

-A 1–2 minute audio introduction

-A response to this scenario:

---“A customer is upset because their appointment needs to be rescheduled. How would you handle the situation?”

-Your internet speed test

title: Remote Leasing Assistant
description:
About Us

Los Angeles property management company managing a large residential portfolio. Our leasing team turns rental applications into clean, owner-ready approval packages. Accuracy and consistency matter enormously — owners make decisions off our write-ups, and a single wrong number or missing verification creates real problems.



The Role

You will process rental applications from start to finish and produce owner-ready “vetted app” packages, following our detailed written SOP exactly. This is precise, checklist-driven work with real judgment: verifying income, reading financial documents, making verification calls, and composing structured summaries that go to property owners for approval.



What You'll Do

? Assemble complete application packages — confirm every adult applicant's ID, application, credit, and background check are present.

? Verify income against our 2.5×-rent threshold, converting pay frequencies correctly and applying our rules for overtime, gig, self-employed, and voucher income.

? Review 3 months of bank statements and the credit report; flag red flags (negative balances, sharp declines, derogatory items) accurately.

? Verify employment and rental history by phone with employers and landlords, and document the results in our standard language.

? Handle Section 8 / Housing Choice Voucher applications — capture voucher details, check bedroom-size match and expiration, and run the alternative income test.

? Compose the vetted-app
 in our exact format and subject-line convention, with correct routing — and catch the common errors before they go out.

? Monitor owner responses and prepare the congratulations letter and internal lease-for-approval once approved.

? Assemble the lease from the approved application and property record, then prepare and send the DocuSign envelope to the correct signer (which varies by property type).

? Monitor the leasing inbox throughout the day — owner approvals, outside-agent messages, and applicant replies — and move each file to its next step promptly.

What We're Looking For

? Exceptional attention to detail. This role lives or dies on accuracy — correct numbers, complete fields, no typos in addresses or figures.

? Strong written English (owner- and applicant-facing
s must be clean and professional) and clear spoken English (you'll call U.S. employers and landlords to verify).

? Comfort with numbers — percentages, pay-frequency conversions, and threshold math done reliably by hand.

? Ability to follow a long, detailed SOP precisely and apply judgment on edge cases rather than guessing.

? Discretion with sensitive financial and personal information.

? Reliable computer, stable internet (?25 Mbps) with a backup connection, and a backup-power plan.

? A plus: experience in property management, leasing, mortgage/loan underwriting, insurance, or BPO back-office work; AppFolio; or familiarity with U.S. Section 8 / HACLA.



How to Apply — Read Carefully

To be considered, your application MUST include all of the following. Applications missing any item will not be reviewed.

1 Internet speed proof. A Speedtest.net screenshot showing at least 25 Mbps download.

2 A quick math check (show your work): The rent is $2,095/month. An applicant's only income is a bi-weekly paycheck with gross pay of $3,391.83. (a) What is the minimum monthly income we require? (b) What is the applicant's monthly income? (c) Do they qualify?

3 A short writing sample. Write a brief, professional
 to an applicant telling them their bank statements were incomplete — you need the 3 most recent statements from one account, as PDFs (not screenshots).

4 Three short answers (a few sentences each): (a) Describe any experience you have reviewing financial documents, verifying information, or processing applications. (b) How do you make sure you don't miss details in repetitive work? (c) Your current internet provider and your backup plan for outages.

5 Your rate. Expected hourly rate in USD and earliest availability.

Why these? The math and writing questions mirror the actual daily work. Strong applications that follow instructions move to a short skills test, a video call, and reference checks.



Our Process

? Application review against the requirements above.

? Short skills test (process a sample rental application into a vetted-app write-up).

? Video interview.

? Reference checks, then offer.

title: # DM Setter & Sales Closer Role
description:
We are looking for a sharp, proactive, and sales-minded DM Setter & Closer to help us manage and convert warm leads for our travel and personal-development offers.



This role is for someone who understands the psychology of sales, knows how to build trust through text conversations, and can confidently guide interested prospects toward the next step.



You will be texting with people who have already shown interest in our products, mainly through text messages, DMs, and
. We have a high volume of leads, so we need someone organized, emotionally intelligent, and consistent.



## Main Responsibilities



* Respond to warm leads through GoHighLevel, text messages, DMs, and

* Start conversations with interested prospects and qualify them properly

* Understand the prospect’s goals, objections, needs, and level of interest

* Follow up consistently with leads until they are ready to book or buy

* Help prospects understand the value of our tours and offers

* Set appointments or close sales directly, depending on the situation

* Keep lead records updated inside GoHighLevel

* Communicate clearly with the team about hot leads, closed deals, and follow-ups

* Maintain a professional, warm, and positive tone in every conversation



## What We Are Looking For



* Experience in sales, appointment setting, closing, or DM sales

* Strong understanding of sales psychology and human behavior

* Excellent written English

* Experience using GoHighLevel is a strong advantage

* Comfortable speaking with leads through text,
, and DMs

* Positive, proactive, and solution-focused attitude

* Organized and consistent with follow-ups

* Able to work independently and take responsibility

* Hungry to grow, improve, and become better at sales

* Someone who is available to work USA Hours





## This Role Is Best For Someone Who



* Loves sales and communication

* Knows how to build trust through conversation

* Can handle objections without being pushy

* Is confident, kind, and professional

* Wants to grow with a fast-moving team

* Can work with a high volume of leads

* Is serious about performance and results



## How To Apply



Please send us a message with:



1. Your past experience in sales, appointment setting, or closing

2. What types of products or services you have sold before

3. Your experience with GoHighLevel or similar CRM platforms

4. A short explanation of why you believe you would be great for this role

5. Your availability and expected compensation



We are looking for someone reliable, motivated, and ready to grow with us.



If this sounds like you, apply now and tell us about your sales experience.

title: Home Care Recruiting Supervisor
description:
(IF YOU DO NOT HAVE PREVIOUS  RECRUITING EXPERIENCE, PLEASE DO NOT APPLY.)



How to Apply:

Please complete the following steps to be considered for this position-

1.) Record a 30-second to 1-minute video introduction** telling us: Your recruiting experience, what your day-to-day responsibilities were in your previous recruiting role(s), and why you believe you would be a great fit for this position.

2.)
 your video to our hiring team: 

3.) Please ensure your face is clearly visible throughout the video, and your audio is clear and easy to understand.





Position: Home Care Recruiter (Remote)



Compensation:

* $1,000 USD per month

* Pesos: 53,240/month



Schedule:

* Full time: Monday - Friday

* Hours: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM HST (Hawaii Standard Time)



About the Position:

title: Dispute Processor
description:

Experience with:

Please submit:
